title: Where is the vibration or noise coming from?
summary: Separate frequency location, throttle dependence, measured motor harmonics, filter boundaries, and downstream residual noise before naming a cause.
questions: Is this energy tied to throttle or measured motor RPM?
What changed between unfiltered gyro, filtered gyro, D term, and motor output?
Are the configured filters acting in the same region as the observed noise?

blocks.text: A tall peak is a location, not a confession. Spectrum lets you ask whether energy stays fixed, follows throttle, follows measured motor speed, survives filtering, or arrives downstream where D term and motors care about it.

steps: Begin with Frequency and compare appropriate signal groups, usually pre-filter gyro, filtered gyro, D term, or motors as available.
Switch to Frequency vs Throttle to see whether ridges move with load.
Use Frequency vs RPM when eRPM was logged; confirm motor pole count before trusting mechanical-frequency alignment.
Overlay recorded filter positions and measured RPM-notch harmonics where available.
Measure a narrower time range if the suspected behaviour was brief.

blocks.title: Read the signal path, not one screenshot

items.title: Locate
items.text: Frequency mode shows where energy is concentrated and compares axes or signal stages. Hanning windowing is available to reduce leakage tradeoffs.

items.title: Relate
items.text: Throttle-dependent ridges are consistent with propulsion-related behaviour; RPM-aligned harmonics are stronger motor evidence when eRPM and pole count are sound.

items.title: Follow downstream
items.text: Compare what enters the filter path with filtered gyro, D term, and motor output. Raw gyro alone can understate the practical effect of residual high-frequency noise.

items.title: Account for delay
items.text: The inspector can estimate gyro, D-term, and total filter delay when the necessary paired signals exist. Less noise and more delay are both real outcomes.

items.title: Return to time
items.text: Use Graph to see whether the band is continuous, manoeuvre-specific, or concentrated around an impact, propwash recovery, or motor anomaly interval.

blocks.expression: motor frequency = logged eRPM × 3.333 ÷ motor poles
blocks.explanation: Airframe follows the current Betaflight conversion used for RPM-notch interpretation. The result is only as credible as the recorded eRPM and configured pole count.

variables.meaning: Electrical RPM value recorded for a motor
The physical motor magnet-pole count configured for conversion

blocks.title: Do not tune from a universal red line
blocks.text: Familiar 50 Hz, -30 dB, -10 dB, and prop-size regions come from particular tools, examples, and craft classes. Airframe presents setup guides as heuristic context and does not convert them into pass/fail. A quiet spectrum also does not prove safe motors. Check temperature and hardware after cautious changes.
